chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

There is no problem with a man entering the state of Ihram in a garment dyed with Mishq, and there is no problem with the one in Ihram changing his clothes. I said, 'If something touches it, he washes it?' He said, 'Yes, and even if he discharges semen in it.'

key_terms.إحرام: The state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.احْتَلَمَ: To discharge semen (via nocturnal emission or otherwise)
key_terms.مِشْقٍ: A specific type of dye, often indigo or black

ai.seo_question: Can a man wear dyed clothes and change garments while in the state of Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the prohibition in Ihram applies to specific types of stitched garments rather than all clothing, explicitly permitting the use of garments dyed with 'Mishq' (a yellow dye from the indigo plant). It further establishes the practical ruling that washing Ihram clothes upon contact with impurities, including seminal discharge, does not break the state of consecration, reflecting the juristic focus on ritual purity over garment material.
